record.paper_title: Observations and Open Questions in Beam-Beam Interactions
record.original_question: Why did KEKB achieve a maximum vertical beam-beam parameter of only 0.09 in the higher-energy ring when beam-beam simulations predicted 0.15, and what mechanisms were limiting further luminosity increase under crab-cavity operation?

evidence.quote: The maximum vertical beam-beam parameter achieved is 0.09 in the higher energy ring as opposed to a predicted value of 0.15 by beam-beam simulations. The reasons for the discrepancy and the limitations on achieving higher luminosity were under active study as of June 2010 [23].

artifact.self_contained_problem: In the KEKB asymmetric electron–positron collider operated with crab cavities, the maximum vertical beam-beam parameter ξ_y achieved experimentally in the higher-energy ring was approximately 0.09, whereas strong–strong and weak–strong beam-beam simulations (with head-on or crab crossing collision and horizontal tune near the half integer) predicted a value of about 0.15. Identify and quantitatively explain the physical mechanisms that caused this discrepancy between the simulated and measured maximum vertical beam-beam parameter, and determine which effects (e.g., parasitic long-range crossings, residual crossing angle errors, lattice nonlinearities, dynamic-aperture/beam-lifetime limitations, electron-cloud effects, optics or coupling errors, noise, or impedance) limited further increases of luminosity under crab-cavity operation.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent KEKB operational reports and review papers (e.g., on crab-cavity operation and the SuperKEKB design study) confirm that the discrepancy between the achieved ξ_y ≈ 0.09 and the simulated ξ_y > 0.1–0.15 was studied but not conclusively explained; SuperKEKB adopted the nano-beam scheme rather than relying on crab crossing partly because of these unresolved limitations. No single agreed-upon mechanism is identified in the available literature, so the question is best characterized as unresolved/partial.

status_evidence.title: Operational experience with crab cavities at KEKB
status_evidence.snippet: Higher specific luminosity than the geometrical gain was achieved with crab cavities, but further study was necessary to reach the prediction of simulation; achieved luminosity and beam lifetime were contradictory to beam-beam simulation.
status_evidence.claim: The discrepancy between simulated and achieved beam-beam parameter at KEKB with crab cavities remained under study and was not fully resolved.

status_evidence.title: Accelerator design at SuperKEKB
status_evidence.snippet: SuperKEKB adopts the nano-beam scheme instead of relying on crab crossing collision used at KEKB.
status_evidence.claim: The KEKB crab-cavity beam-beam limitation motivated a different design approach for SuperKEKB, indicating the original limitation was not overcome at KEKB.
